I do agree that it's not really a problem, but here are the two issues

1. Wrong detection: The request pending detection is mostly wrong - because actually, the follows go through (both public and private)

2. When it is detected, Follow tool automatically gets disabled - and has to be manually re-enabled (biggest problem)


An example of a case where pending request is wrong:
The bot attempts to follow an user - but the pop up "Review this account before following" pops up

WHY THIS WORKS (Short Bullets)
    •    ✅ Strips all metadata
→ Removes hidden tags, titles, timestamps Meta could match against.
    •    ✅ Slight crop + scale back
→ Shifts pixels, breaks spatial alignment Meta’s hash depends on.
    •    ✅ Random brightness/saturation tweak
→ Alters color histogram so visual fingerprint changes.
    •    ✅ Adds invisible noise
→ Breaks per-frame pixel patterns; each frame becomes unique.
    •    ✅ Slight speed + pitch change (±2–4%)
→ Desyncs both visual timeline & audio waveform — kills frame and audio fingerprinting.
    •    ✅ Optional black padding intro/outro
→ Shifts entire content timeline, throws off start-aligned hashes.
    •    ✅ Randomized per copy
→ No two copies are the same — even Meta can’t confidently cluster them.
    •    ✅ Uses clean H.264 + AAC
→ Fully compatible with IG/Threads and avoids reprocessing quirks that leak identity.

content: To summarize the process, ThreatExchange fights duplicates by converting every image or video into a perceptual hash, a tiny numeric “fingerprint” that captures overall visual structure instead of exact pixels. For photos it uses PDQ, which runs a discrete-cosine transform on a normalized, grayscale copy of the picture, thresholds the low-frequency coefficients, then stores the resulting 256-bit binary pattern; two images are considered the same when the Hamming distance between their hashes falls below a chosen threshold. For video it offers TMK + PDQF and the lighter vPDQ: they generate PDQ-style hashes for individual frames, then feed those through a temporal-match kernel that summarises frame order and content into a fixed-length vector (≈256 KB). Hash vectors are compared with fast cosine or Hamming distance searches, making matches robust to compression, scaling, crops or brief edits. The repo’s Hasher-Matcher-Actioner service stores known hashes, scans incoming media in real time, and triggers whatever policy you define the moment a duplicate (or near-duplicate) score crosses your threshold.
This is metas open source library for duplicate content detection

I think right now older apk's still work on android 11 or lower, even though safetynet, the predecessor to play integrity, has been sunset and returns an error when called.  App cloner and nomix can spoof it. Spoofing safetynet while google sunsets Safetynet means that either Insta knows you are using a clone and doesn't care about it or more likely that there is no build in expiration date on the safetynet attestation on your apk and the app still runs.

Instagram can check with an SQL query which apps that have safetynet still shoot mobile api requests to their server and block each and every one of them. Alternativley they can cutoff requests based on apk version to their servers.

Then there is the whole issue about Device Integrity which is part of the play integrity check for the apk, but this is only an issue if you root.

TLDR: time is running out on solutions that don't have a fix for play integrity, hence nomix futureproof with the visibility we have today

If anyone has the problem that when downloading the Google Sheet document, where there are texts in English that use: ´ and when downloading to the PC in Excel it turns into strange symbols, it is because of the UTF-8 encoding. I leave you the steps to be able to obtain the document correctly and then upload it to Onimator:

Open Excel (without opening the CSV document yet).
Go to Data → Get External Data → From Text/CSV File.
Select the CSV file and click Import.
In the import window:
Select "Comma Delimited".
Under "File Source", choose UTF-8.
Click Upload.
Then save the document to CSV and you can upload it to Onimator.

✅ This will ensure that special characters are displayed correctly.

As a SW architect with a good bit of experience, I've got some ideas to make that tool more efficient, especially for engaging with many users daily.
First - cache data about accounts we've already interacted with to avoid repeating (different or same) actions on the same profile.
For example, follow one account and like another's posts instead of doing both on the same account.

Second - for skipping specific names, it would be helpful if we could set patterns that automatically skip any account containing certain strings.
Like if we add "Rohan" to our skip list, any account with "Rohan" in the name gets bypassed.
